narratives.Description: BLOCKER: one-PR-unit story-readiness cannot resolve durable grants (0.119.7)
narratives.Overview:
1. The ordinary verify:story-ready path calls resolveProductionAppStore, the same resolver human mint uses. When that result is ok, the resolved store is passed into loadOnePrUnitGrant. This path does not call getDefaultAppStore and does not use the mint helper that returns the in-memory store when the resolver is not ok. The in-memory store remains an explicit test seam.
2. resolveProductionAppStore is ok only when DEFT_ONE_PR_UNIT_APP is an absolute path that is already a directory, or the same mkdir the store uses to create that directory succeeds. A relative path, the forbidden .deft/one-pr-unit path, and a failed create are configuration failures. Directory ancestry is not the acceptance condition. Mint and story-ready both use that result. A projectRoot base is not the store identity.
3. A resolver failure is surfaced as the resolver message and does not fall through to the missing-grant sentence. Readiness does not ask for another mint on that failure. The missing-grant sentence remains only after the resolver has returned ok and the grant is absent. A directory with no claims.json, including a directory this check just created, stays the missing-grant result.
4. Offline closing-keyword lookup, closeout attestation, and the merge-group default stay on the in-memory default until a later fix or an explicit unsupported note. This contract is the verify:story-ready path.
5. Exact-set comparison, the human-origin check, and PR-node binding stay as they are. Declare does not receive a pull-request node id. The opaque id stays a lookup key.

audit-targets: none

The refutation target survives only after the statement adds two constraints. As written, a second verify:story-ready process still evaluates an empty store. No blocking finding. HEAD is c7cae4d44e40abf4fb00ee25aceacf32d06168d9. The in-envelope thread is comment 5794367773.

## Absolute store directory
sharpens-framing
Evidence: git show c7cae4d44e40abf4fb00ee25aceacf32d06168d9:packages/core/src/one-pr-unit/store.ts. resolveProductionAppStore returns ok and constructs DirectiveGitHubAppStore for any value that is non-empty, not an in-process marker, and not a .deft/one-pr-unit path. The constructor sets this.root = resolve(root) from node:path. Nothing under packages/core/src/one-pr-unit checks isAbsolute. loadOnePrUnitGrant ignores its projectRoot argument. packages/cli/src/verify-story-ready.ts run() passes projectRoot and does not pass a store. tasks/verify.yml launches that CLI with --project-root set to the user working directory. On this host, Node path.resolve('rel-store') from two working directories produced two directories; one absolute path produced one directory.
Failure mode: Mint and story-ready can both accept DEFT_ONE_PR_UNIT_APP and still open different claims.json files when the value is relative and the working directories differ. A dest worktree, or any second process whose cwd is not the mint cwd, hydrates an empty store. getById returns null. story-ready/evaluate.ts then returns SOLO_MULTI_COHORT_CONFIG, which tells the operator to mint again. The resolver already returned ok, so the miss stays an empty store.
Disposition: Before bind, the resolver must reject a relative DEFT_ONE_PR_UNIT_APP as a configuration failure, and mint and story-ready must both use that result. The shared directory is an absolute path. A projectRoot base changes with each worktree, so it does not identify one store.

## Fail-closed authz result
sharpens-framing
Evidence: packages/cli/src/authz.ts, the one-pr-unit template, calls resolveProductionAppStore, returns exit 2 with resolved.message when ok is false, and passes resolved.store into mintOnePrUnitGrant. packages/core/src/one-pr-unit/mint.ts mintStoreFromEnv returns getDefaultAppStore() when that resolver is not ok. simulator.ts initializes the default as new InProcessAppStore(). git grep at this SHA finds setDefaultAppStore only at its definition. story-ready/evaluate.ts calls loadOnePrUnitGrant(projectRoot, grantId) with no store, and a null grant returns SOLO_MULTI_COHORT_CONFIG from types.ts, including the mint-an-operator-origin sentence. store.test.ts requires the not-configured message to avoid that sentence. verify-story-ready run() does not pass onePrUnitGrant.
Failure mode: Reusing mintStoreFromEnv, or resolving a store and then falling through the null-grant return, keeps the in-memory default. The operator gets a mint request. That request is already exit code 2, so labeling the miss a configuration failure leaves the text unchanged. setDefaultAppStore cannot close the gap: the default is an in-memory singleton, and a second process starts from InProcessAppStore again.
Disposition: Before bind, the ordinary CLI path must follow the authz branch. Surface the resolver failure message, and pass the resolved store into loadOnePrUnitGrant. The mint text remains the missing-grant result only after the resolver has returned ok. The in-memory default remains the explicit test seam.

## Other default-store callers
footnote
Evidence: At this SHA, pr-closing-keywords/main.ts calls resolveProductionAppStore on the live PR path and calls loadOnePrUnitGrant with no store on the offline path. pr-closeout-attestable/evaluate.ts calls loadOnePrUnitGrant(root, id) with no store. merge-group-cli.ts main() calls runMergeGroupCheckFromEvent with no store, so the seam is getDefaultAppStore().
Failure mode: Those paths still miss a grant written by human mint, if a later reader treats this premise as covering every load.
Disposition: No change to this premise. The sentence is the verify:story-ready path. Those callers stay on the default until a later fix or an explicit unsupported note. The issue text already allows that split.

## Missing claims file
footnote
Evidence: DirectiveGitHubAppStore.hydrate returns an empty in-memory store when claims.json is absent, and getById then returns null. A fresh absolute directory has no claims file until the first successful mint persist.
Failure mode: Treating a missing claims file as an invalid backend makes a not-yet-minted directory the same diagnostic as a bad path and collapses the missing-grant case into configuration.
Disposition: No existence check. After the resolver returns ok, a miss stays the missing-grant result.

## Bound grant on a later readiness run
footnote
Evidence: classifyAllocation calls evaluateOnePrUnit with phase declare and binding { repo: options.onePrUnitRepo }. verify-story-ready run() does not set onePrUnitRepo. The evaluator returns deny-not-bearer when grant.prNodeId is set and the presented node id is empty. Human mint writes state reserved with prNodeId null, which declare allows.
Failure mode: A readiness rerun after the grant is bound fails closed even when the store hit is real.
Disposition: No change for the reserved unbound grant this premise covers. Supplying a PR node id to declare would blur declare and enforce.

## Claims-file trust
footnote
Evidence: DirectiveGitHubAppStore persists claims.json under the configured directory. evaluateOnePrUnit checks origin.kind on that record. The live PR path already runs enforceLiveOnePrUnitCheck against this store.
Failure mode: A process that can write the claims file can present an operator-origin record. Readiness trusts the same file the live check already trusts.
Disposition: No new identity control. Exact-set comparison and the human-origin check stay as they are. The opaque id stays a lookup key.

## In plain English

This is a design audit, not a claim that the proposed repair has been implemented or passed an end-to-end test.

## P2: An absolute non-directory backend still becomes a missing grant
blocks-the-design

Evidence: At the pinned SHA, packages/core/src/one-pr-unit/store.ts resolveProductionAppStore rejects empty values, simulator selections, and the forbidden .deft/one-pr-unit path, then constructs DirectiveGitHubAppStore. Its constructor resolves the path; hydrate checks existsSync(join(root, "claims.json")) and returns an empty InProcessAppStore when false. It does not establish that an existing root is a directory. The Bound remedy adds rejection of relative paths, but does not address this absolute-path case; item 3 expressly leaves a missing claims file after ok as the missing-grant result.

Check performed: In the OS temp directory, created an ordinary file named backend-file and probed it with Node's filesystem/path APIs. Result: absolute=true, rootIsFile=true, claimsExists=false. Removed the probe file and directory afterward. This checks the decisive filesystem branch; the resolver/readiness consequence is source-traced, not a full CLI execution.

Concrete failure: Set DEFT_ONE_PR_UNIT_APP to that absolute file path and run the solo multi-scope readiness path with a grant id. Even with items 1-3 implemented, the relative-path check passes, the resolver returns ok with an empty store, getById returns null, and story-ready/evaluate.ts returns SOLO_MULTI_COHORT_CONFIG. The operator is asked to mint again even though the configured backend cannot be a store directory. Human mint cannot repair that configuration by writing a grant there.

Disposition: The P2 cite cannot bind as written. Distinguish an invalid existing backend root from a valid directory with no claims file before selecting missing-grant remediation. This does not require rejecting a fresh, not-yet-created store directory or treating every absent claims file as configuration failure. No new store or identity mechanism is needed.

## P1: Explicit durable lookup closes the process-local visibility gap
footnote

Pinned-source evidence: authz.ts already resolves the production store and passes resolved.store to mintOnePrUnitGrant. store.ts persists claims.json and rehydrates it on getById. story-ready/evaluate.ts currently omits the store argument to loadOnePrUnitGrant, whose default is getDefaultAppStore. Bound-remedy items 1-2 replace precisely that default lookup and require the same absolute directory across working directories. For the valid reserved, unbound grant in scope, the P1 cite holds. This conclusion is conditional on implementing that wiring and does not substitute for the issue's cross-process regression.

## Shared-state and authority boundary
footnote

The remedy keeps the configured durable store as the existing trust boundary. The pinned evaluateOnePrUnit checks human origin, lifecycle and exact origin-set equality; declaration permits a reserved unbound claim, while a bound claim still requires its PR node. Bound-remedy item 5 preserves those checks. Reading the durable record does not make the opaque id a bearer credential. Offline/default-store callers remain explicitly outside this remedy. These observations do not change the harvest or cure the P2 finding.

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

In published Directive **0.119.7**, the human-only one-PR-unit mint resolves the durable backend, but the normal `verify:story-ready` path still loads the grant from the process-local `InProcessAppStore`. A separate readiness process therefore cannot see the durable grant through its default lookup path.

This is a **leftover of #4635 / PR #4683**, not a request to relax exact-set consent or PR-node binding. PR #4683 repaired minting and live PR enforcement but did not change the story-readiness caller.

## Affected flow and consumer impact

- Consumer: `deftai/BestiMax`, on macOS/zsh.
- Inspected published CLI/core version: **0.119.7**; the prepared adoption pins the CLI/core/content/types family to that version.
- Flow: operator-approved solo integration of two active issue scopes into one atomic PR, with `cohort_vbriefs` containing both scopes and an exact-set `one_pr_unit_id`.
- Work blocked: combining https://github.com/deftai/BestiMax/issues/402 and https://github.com/deftai/BestiMax/issues/408. The first repairs required-check composition; the second adopts the compatible Directive family. Reversible combined validation passed locally, but implementation dispatch is stopped at grant/readiness authorization.
- The consumer shell also lacks `DEFT_ONE_PR_UNIT_APP`. That is a separate configuration prerequisite, **not evidence of the wiring defect**. Setting it alone does not connect the readiness loader to the durable backend.

## Versioned code trace

These are line numbers in the published 0.119.7 JavaScript, not assertions about current upstream HEAD:

1. `@deftai/directive/dist/authz.js:428-459`: the `one-pr-unit` template calls `resolveProductionAppStore(process.env)` and passes `resolved.store` to `mintOnePrUnitGrant`.
2. `@deftai/directive/dist/verify-story-ready.js`: `run()` calls the story-ready evaluator with project/allocation context but no injected grant or durable store.
3. `@deftai/directive-core/dist/story-ready/evaluate.js:124-130`: for solo dispatch with more than one scope, the evaluator calls `loadOnePrUnitGrant(options.projectRoot, grantId)`.
4. `@deftai/directive-core/dist/one-pr-unit/store.js:21`: `loadOnePrUnitGrant(_projectRoot, grantId, store = getDefaultAppStore())` reads that default store.
5. `@deftai/directive-core/dist/one-pr-unit/simulator.js:261-270`: the default is `new InProcessAppStore()`. A scan of both packages' shipped JavaScript found the `setDefaultAppStore` definition but no callers.

Source counterparts: `packages/cli/src/authz.ts`, `packages/cli/src/verify-story-ready.ts`, `packages/core/src/story-ready/evaluate.ts`, and `packages/core/src/one-pr-unit/{store,simulator}.ts`.

## Read-only reproducer

In a scratch environment with the exact 0.119.7 packages installed, run:

```js
// Run with: node --input-type=module
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { onePrUnit } from "@deftai/directive-core";

const path = join(tmpdir(), "directive-readonly-lookup-" + randomUUID());
const resolved = onePrUnit.resolveProductionAppStore({
  DEFT_ONE_PR_UNIT_APP: path,
});
console.log(JSON.stringify({
  productionResolution: resolved.ok,
  configuredBackend: resolved.ok
    ? resolved.store.constructor.name
    : resolved.code,
  defaultLookupBackend: onePrUnit.getDefaultAppStore().constructor.name,
  directoryCreated: existsSync(path),
}));
```

Observed against the exact published package, using an absolute package import in the isolated installation:

```json
{"productionResolution":true,"configuredBackend":"DirectiveGitHubAppStore","defaultLookupBackend":"InProcessAppStore","directoryCreated":false}
```

This probe neither mints a grant nor creates the directory. Combined with the normal CLI call trace above, it shows that resolving a configured backend does not change the store used by default readiness lookup.

**Evidence limit:** no real human mint, configured deployment, valid-grant cross-process CLI acceptance test, or live PR enforcement test was performed in the consumer session. The readiness failure for a separately minted durable grant is a source-traced consequence, not a claimed end-to-end production run.

## Expected behavior

The normal readiness CLI should resolve the same supported durable backend as human minting, then evaluate the actual exact-set operator grant. Missing or invalid backend configuration should produce a configuration diagnostic rather than silently consulting an empty simulator and asking the operator to mint again.

Local declaration/readiness must remain distinct from live PR enforcement: the opaque ID is a lookup key, not a bearer; immutable PR-node binding and the existing exact-set, lifecycle and human-presence checks must remain intact.

## Acceptance criteria

- Wire the ordinary `verify:story-ready` CLI/evaluator path to the configured durable store without requiring caller-side test injection or monkey-patching.
- Add an isolated cross-process regression: a valid operator-origin test fixture is persisted in process A; process B invokes the actual readiness CLI with matching active scopes and allocation context and successfully resolves it.
- Retain negative coverage for missing/invalid configuration, missing or invalid grants, and mismatched origin sets. Do not weaken human-only minting or live PR-node enforcement.
- Audit other default `loadOnePrUnitGrant` consumers, including offline closing-keyword checks and closeout attestation, for the same fallback; fix or explicitly document any remaining unsupported path.
- Keep in-memory stores explicit test dependencies rather than the silent production fallback for configured flows.

## Alternatives and recovery cost

- A supported backend plus a real operator mint is necessary, but not sufficient while readiness reads a different store.
- Simulator injection, fabricated grant files, installed-verifier patches, changing references to hide the second origin, and weakening gates are not acceptable recovery paths.
- Independently merging the two prerequisites would abandon the operator-approved atomic-delivery requirement.
- Current recovery cost: the two reviewed local candidates remain parked; additional upstream repair/release validation is needed before integration can resume. No elapsed-time estimate or universal outage claim is asserted.

## Related work and duplicate check

Refs #4635, #4683, #4494, #1709.

Searches for open one-PR-unit reports, `loadOnePrUnitGrant`, and `InProcessAppStore` found no open report of this readiness-specific leftover. The prior issue body and all comments were reviewed; PR #4683 merged on 2026-09-17 as `6d4e12d5566521ad9584539f2a44d7fe216e8854`.

Filed at the consumer operator's explicit request. `BLOCKER` describes the affected consumer flow; it is not a request to infer or automatically apply the privileged `adoption-blocker` label.
